title: One-minute test cut: Void, First Stirring, Parabrahman, Desire, Om
anchor_convention: t = absolute seconds from voice_timeline.md. 'word' = the spoken word at that time. If 'edge':'end' is present, t is the END of that word/line (line end times from the timeline) instead of its start.

first_stirring.note: two close notes and an open, unresolved fifth; high register (D5-D6) so it stays out of the voice pocket. Returns transposed (A) and faster at the vibration, and fed into Om.

eternal_parabrahman.note: bare open fifth, no third, then the Yaman raised 4th glows over it. Formless, no pulse.

desire_ichha.note: rising bansuri line, last 1 = upper Sa. Hint [3,5] on first 'ichha', full phrase on the last.

om.note: low Sa, Pa, Sa: a slow open-fifth bloom. Resolves the stirring (1 and 5 are shared, the unresolved 2 is gone).

danger_shadow.note: root plus flat 2nd cluster, low and quiet; foreshadows Madhu-Kaitabha.

cues.note: Void. Tanpura on Sa-Sa (no Pa, malkauns), very slow plucks, almost nothing.
Cosmic hum under the whole of beat 1; sinks to about intensity 1 inside silence c04 and c07.
Dark open-D sub pad swells slowly during the negations (no sun, no moon, no day, no night), then is cut for the silence.
Drop-out before 'कुछ भी नहीं' (Nothing). Pad and tanpura stop; only the faintest hum remains. The emptiest moment of the piece.
Tanpura plucks return after the silence: something is about to happen.
Slow reverse swell, low (D1 rising to D3) plus a thin airy top, below 250 Hz until the last second. Peak intensity 5 at the cut.
Everything stops one beat before the biggest word. Only a single held high D (celesta-like glass tone) and the faintest hum. 'पहली बार... कुछ' is spoken into near silence.
FIRST STIRRING: one soft sub boom with a long low tail (all energy below 150 Hz). Not a jump scare, a heartbeat of the universe.
FIRST STIRRING motif, statement 1, played an octave up (D5-D6), sparse and soft so it does not fight the word. Memorable open ending on the fifth.
Soft low heartbeat, the first pulse of life, runs through beat 2. Dies away in the pause at 28.90 so that Parabrahman has no pulse.
Low string pad, thin above 250 Hz. Sets up the narrator's promise, uneasy rather than frightening.
Birth of creation: first glimpse of Yaman light, a short choir ooh swell that blooms in the tiny gap after 'हुआ।'.
DANGER shadow: low brass root plus flat-2nd cluster, quiet, the first dark colour after the light of c12.
Tremolo bed under 'सृष्टि के साथ ही पैदा हो गया था', creeping dread.
Everything cut (strings, heartbeat, brass); only the tanpura of c16 rings. Clean reset into the new mood and the new mode (Yaman).
Tanpura on Sa-Pa for the whole of Parabrahman, desire and vibration. The constant, it is the 'one truth'. It is also the held tone in the silences c18 and c26.
Quiet organ open fifth, almost not there, preparing the reveal.
Drop-out one beat before the big word 'परब्रह्म'. Only the tanpura.
ETERNAL motif: open-fifth choir with organ blooms on the word and swells through the 0.70 s pause (34.40 to 35.10), then thins under 'जिसका'.
One soft deep gong on 'परब्रह्म', the first sacred sound. (Shankh is kept for Om.)
Brahma-style sustained choir/organ pad, no pulse, no rhythm. Slow chord changes (about every 4.6 s) for 'no beginning, no end, beyond thought'.
Glass shimmer rising away: 'beyond thought'.
Second, slightly higher shimmer: 'beyond the senses'.
Slow harp arpeggio: infinite possibilities asleep.
Quiet rising string ostinato plus reverse swell, the pull of a desire forming (peak 5 at the cut).
DESIRE motif, hint: just the first two notes, held, lower-register bansuri, very soft.
Drop-out one beat before the biggest word of the beat. Riser and pad stop; only tanpura. 'बस एक' lands in a held breath.
DESIRE motif, full rising phrase, ends on upper Sa which is the seed of Om.
Soft timpani and sub on the word 'इच्छा': the wish becomes a force.
Warm string pad crescendo (4 to 6), the cosmos about to speak.
FIRST STIRRING returns: now the vibration. Transposed up a fifth (A), faster, in Yaman colour; the audience recognises it.
Second statement, an octave higher and quicker, still unresolved: it needs the Om to answer it.
Low timpani roll crescendo (3 to 6), the vibration building.
Reverse swell and rising choir, low-weighted; hard cut at the word 'ध्वनि' for the silence.
BIGGEST DROP-OUT: everything stops, tanpura included (c16 ends here). 'ध्वनि...' hangs in dry silence for about 1 s before Om.
OM IMPACT: deep sub boom (D1) with a long tail through the 1.10 s pause. The biggest hit of the cut.
Large gong blooming under the boom.
Conch on the Om: the series sacred sound enters in its full-power moment.
OM motif at full width (choir plus voice oohs plus sub) in the 1.10 s gap. Memorable: low Sa, Pa, Sa, a blooming open fifth. Full range allowed here.
Om drone continues under the final line, choir with organ; pulled about 7 dB under voice. Rises slightly toward the end (5 to 6).
Rising arpeggio layers, every sound of the world inside Om.
One soft temple bell: the first 'worldly' sound born inside Om.
SERIES LOGO SOUND at the end: tanpura plus conch plus low boom (c42, c43, c44) after the last word. Needs 3 s of tail past 68.4 s (see requests).
Low boom of the logo.
Tanpura rings out with the Om drone dissolving into it.

requests: Logo/end tail: allow about 3 s of audio after the last voice sample (68.4 s to about 71.3 s) for c42-c44. If the video must stay 68.4 s, fade the logo out at 68.4 s.
Series logo at the start is NOT placed because the voice starts at 0.10 s. Optionally add 1.5 s of pre-roll with tanpura plus conch plus low boom, shifting all times by +1.5 s.
Sub boom and gong tails must be low-passed or carry no content above 150 Hz when they run under speech (c08, c28).
Sidechain: duck all music 4-6 dB under speech (duck_db values above), bigger release in the gaps listed in the brief.
Santoor / glass tone (c09, c30, c31, c07) should sit an octave up (D5-D6) to stay out of the voice pocket.
Degree 1 upper-Sa in c27 and the semitone cluster in c13 (root plus flat 2nd) may need explicit note numbers if the engine reads degrees only 1-7.
